title: I made a browser 3D rhythm game where you fly through any song – even live from YouTube or Spotify. 100% code by Claude, music by Suno
author: GurusCZ
selftext:
I've been working on Fly Through Your Music – a 3D rhythm game that runs right in the browser (Three.js). The world is generated from the music and reacts to the beat. You can:

\- drop in your own MP3/WAV/OGG file,

\- play live from another tab – YouTube, Spotify Web or SoundCloud (desktop Chrome/Edge, via tab audio sharing),

\- or pick one of the built-in tracks.

It works on phones too, with touch controls, and there's a "reduce flashing" option for anyone sensitive to flashing lights.

▶️ Link in comment

![img](uhy4uh86e8xh1 "actual gameplay")

![img](heohu9m7e8xh1 "actual gameplay 2")

How AI was involved:

\- Code: written entirely by Claude. I described the mechanics and visuals, tested, gave feedback, and iterated – I didn't write the code myself. This isn't a one-prompt game.

\- Workflow: I work with Claude in VS Code; the game was made with Opus 5.5 on medium effort. I start with a plan, and after each milestone I commit, test what was done, then /clear the chat and move on to the next one. That keeps the context window under \~150k.

\- Music: two tracks made with Suno – one created specifically for this game, the other from another game I'm working on.

It's still a work in progress, so I'd love feedback – especially on how the gameplay feels, mainly the controls and difficulty. Would you play it more with your own songs or with the built-in tracks?
